notes: Summary: ShearWave is a programmatic adtech platform doing real-time bid scoring and reranking across user sessions. Main constraint: high QPS with tight p99 latency (goal <30ms end-to-end for scoring step).

Workload profile: short-context chat-style prompts for personalization (avg tokens per request ~60), large fraction of requests are cacheable (same user segments), spikes aligned with campaign events (1.5-2x), overall throughput target for POC: 5k req/s sustained, burst to 12k req/s.
Perf targets: p50 <8ms, p95 <20ms, p99 <30ms for generation+scoring; tail tolerance low (business SLA). Cost sensitivity: target <$0.0004 per inference request (important for margin).

Optimize interest: strong focus on batching policy tuning, prefix/KV caching to keep KV hit rate high, and evaluating quantization (int8 / 4-bit) tradeoffs for cost vs latency vs quality. Want Redwood Optimize recommendations and automated quant profiles for their model family.

Model preferences: prefer open LLM variants for on-prem control (llama-derivatives, mix of FP16 and quantized), but open to Redwood-managed hosted variants for initial rollout. Need controlled fallbacks when quantization affects quality.

Security / compliance: VPC-only control plane for demo, SSO (SAML) for teams, KMS for envelope encryption, audit logs for all inference calls, EU data residency for a subset of campaigns (later phase).
Quote from Head of Infrastructure: "If we can't reduce p99 by at least 25% versus our current infra with similar cost, we won't move to managed. Show us batching & cache wins."

POC scope requested by customer: benchmarking matrix across batching window sizes (5-50ms), cache TTL and prefix caching effectiveness, quantization matrix (fp16, int8, int4) on both A100 and T4-like instances, and throughput scaling tests with canary fallback to smaller models.

Preferred deliverables: perf dashboard with per-route p50/p95/p99, token-level cost breakdown, and regression alerts linked to a prompt set. Want Redwood to run 48h side-by-side perf runs vs their in-house stack.
Internal notes: emphasize Redwood's automatic batching/caching heuristics and Optimize's suggested quant profiles. Highlight unified API so switching from hosted->dedicated->private is low friction.
